BN_policy: recalibrate submitted/expected parameters on one clean local training pass; no optimizer
hypothesis: R02: Correcting the confirmed algorithm/phase discrepancies and declaring the IBA integration before training permits a valid test of suppressed pre-FU behavior; success is not assumed.
new_observable: Actual phase order, epoch/batch counts, optimizer boundaries, tested/submitted gamma, same trained generator and exact aggregation are linked to every saved round.
non_iid_scope: This is attack implementation reproduction under the paper default IID profile. It does not resolve D08's large benign non-IID counterexample and makes no detection claim.
stopping_rules: Preserve and stop on source hash mismatch, nonfinite state, broken model chain or exact aggregation mismatch
Preserve and stop if gamma0 expected aggregation fails the strict10pct local criterion
Preserve and stop if gamma search remains feasible at the finite cap10
Preserve and stop after three consecutive post-warmup full-test ASR values above10pct
No automatic post/control branches; final clean utility and fixed10000/9000 evaluation are required before considering any later stage
implementation_choices_not_author_certif: FUBA paper does not uniquely specify how IBA's weighted dual loss and30pct sample portion combine. Use the pinned IBA author's clean-all/poison-subset implementation with alpha.3/beta.7, declared before any outcome
IBA epsilon decay.001 is copied from the pinned IBA author CIFAR script; five warmup rounds are retained from FUBA public defaults. Epsilon0.3 and floor/evaluation0.05 are from the FUBA supplement
Use reported experimental Adam.001 despite SGD in the FUBA derivation
BN recalibration is an explicit engineering policy for parameter displacement, motivated by the saved-model buffer diagnosis; the paper has no BN-buffer rule
Gamma upper bound10 is a finite operational bound; hitting it terminates rather than claiming an unbounded optimum
One seed/one IID cohort is not the paper's ten-seed mean or a verified pre/post unlearning pair
